tests.what_it_measures: Haemoglobin is the iron-rich protein inside red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is part of a complete blood count and is used to look for anaemia and to monitor conditions that affect red blood cells.
tests.general_interpretation_high: A haemoglobin result above the printed interval is interpreted together with the red-cell count, haematocrit and your clinical context rather than on its own.
tests.general_interpretation_low: A haemoglobin result below the printed interval is commonly described as low. MedlinePlus notes that abnormal red-cell, haemoglobin or haematocrit levels may be a sign of dehydration, anaemia, heart disease or too little iron, and that other factors can affect results.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.
Haemoglobin can be affected by hydration and by factors such as diet, activity, medicines and menstruation (MedlinePlus).

tests.what_it_measures: White blood cells are part of the immune system and help the body fight infection and other diseases; a complete blood count measures the total number in a volume of blood.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is used in routine checks and to monitor infections, immune conditions and treatments that affect blood cells.
tests.general_interpretation_high: A high total white-cell count is described by MedlinePlus as possibly related to infection, autoimmune or inflammatory disorders, leukaemia or other cancers, allergic reactions or certain steroids.
tests.general_interpretation_low: A low total white-cell count is described by MedlinePlus as possibly related to bone-marrow disease, chemotherapy, certain medicines, cancer or HIV, among other causes.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.
MedlinePlus notes that abnormal white-cell results do not always mean a condition that needs treatment; injury, stress, smoking and alcohol can also affect the count.

tests.why_it_is_ordered: They are reported as part of a white-cell differential, which can help investigate an infection or an immune condition.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.

A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.

tests.what_it_measures: Haematocrit is the amount of whole blood that is made up of red blood cells.

A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.
Haematocrit can be affected by hydration, as with haemoglobin (MedlinePlus).

tests.what_it_measures: MCV measures the average size of your red blood cells.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is one of the red-cell indices and helps clinicians classify types of anaemia.
tests.general_interpretation_high: MedlinePlus describes larger-than-usual red cells as possibly related to vitamin B deficiency or liver disease, among other causes.
tests.general_interpretation_low: MedlinePlus describes smaller-than-usual red cells as possibly related to iron-deficiency anaemia or thalassaemia, among other causes.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.

tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is one of the red-cell indices used to classify anaemia.
tests.general_interpretation_high: MedlinePlus describes a higher-than-usual MCH as possibly related to anaemia from vitamin B deficiency.
tests.general_interpretation_low: MedlinePlus describes a lower-than-usual MCH as possibly related to iron-deficiency anaemia.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.

tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is one of the red-cell indices used to classify anaemia.
tests.general_interpretation_high: MedlinePlus describes a higher-than-usual MCHC as possibly related to haemolytic anaemia or hereditary spherocytosis.
tests.general_interpretation_low: MedlinePlus describes a lower-than-usual MCHC as possibly related to iron-deficiency anaemia or thalassaemia.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.

tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is part of a complete blood count and is usually interpreted with the other red-cell indices.

MedlinePlus notes that RDW alone is not enough to make a diagnosis and is combined with other results.

tests.what_it_measures: TSH is a hormone made by the pituitary gland that tells the thyroid how much thyroid hormone to make.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is used to find out how well the thyroid is working.

tests.what_it_measures: HbA1c measures the percentage of red blood cells that have glucose attached to their haemoglobin, which reflects average blood glucose over the past two to three months.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is used to screen for or monitor diabetes and prediabetes.
tests.general_interpretation_high: MedlinePlus describes results of 6.5% or higher in the reference categories it lists for diabetes, and notes that providers usually use more than one test before diagnosing diabetes.
tests.general_interpretation_low: MedlinePlus describes results below about 5.7% in the general reference categories it lists, and notes that what is normal for you depends on your health, age and other factors.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.
MedlinePlus notes that conditions affecting red blood cells, kidney failure and liver disease can make HbA1c less reliable.
The ranges MedlinePlus lists are described there as a guide, not a diagnosis; your report may use different categories.

tests.what_it_measures: Prothrombin time measures how many seconds it takes for a clot to form in a blood sample.

tests.what_it_measures: INR is a ratio calculated from the prothrombin time that makes results easier to compare between laboratories and test methods.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is most often used to monitor anticoagulant treatment such as warfarin and to investigate unusual bleeding or clotting.
tests.general_interpretation_high: MedlinePlus explains that an INR that is too high may mean blood is taking longer than normal to clot, and that a provider may change treatment based on the result.
tests.general_interpretation_low: MedlinePlus explains that an INR that is too low may mean blood clots too easily, and that a provider may change treatment based on the result.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.
INR interpretation depends on whether you take an anticoagulant and on the target range your provider set; the printed interval is not the same as a treatment target.

tests.what_it_measures: A vitamin D test measures how much vitamin D is circulating in the blood. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and supports bones, muscles, nerves and the immune system. Results are often reported as total vitamin D, or separately as vitamin D2 and vitamin D3.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is usually ordered when a clinician suspects too little or too much vitamin D — for example with bone pain, muscle weakness, low bone density or a condition that affects vitamin D absorption.
tests.general_interpretation_high: A high vitamin D result is interpreted together with supplements and medical history; very high levels usually reflect intake rather than a disease found by the test alone.
tests.general_interpretation_low: A low result may reflect limited sun exposure, low intake or poor absorption, but the printed interval and the clinical context decide how it is interpreted.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.
This explanation is general education, not a diagnosis; discuss the result with the clinician who ordered it.

tests.what_it_measures: A uric acid test measures the amount of uric acid in blood or urine. Uric acid is a normal waste product made when the body breaks down purines, which come from cells and from some foods.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is often ordered when someone has symptoms of gout, kidney stones, or another condition associated with unusual uric acid levels.
tests.general_interpretation_high: A high blood uric acid result can occur when the body makes too much uric acid or when the kidneys remove too little; diet also affects it.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.
This explanation is general education, not a diagnosis; discuss the result with the clinician who ordered it.

tests.what_it_measures: Iron tests measure substances in the blood that describe iron status, such as serum iron, the iron-binding capacity of transferrin and the percentage of transferrin that is saturated.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: They are ordered when iron deficiency or iron overload is suspected, or when anaemia needs to be characterised.
tests.general_interpretation_high: A high iron result can reflect increased iron stores or recent iron intake; it is interpreted with the other iron tests, not alone.
tests.general_interpretation_low: A low iron result may reflect low stores or an ongoing demand for iron; the pattern across the iron tests matters more than one value.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.
This explanation is general education, not a diagnosis; discuss the result with the clinician who ordered it.

tests.what_it_measures: A microalbumin creatinine ratio test compares the amount of albumin in a urine sample with the amount of creatinine, which adjusts for how concentrated the urine is. Albumin is a protein that should mostly stay in the blood.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It is usually ordered when someone is at higher risk of kidney disease — for example with diabetes or high blood pressure — because early kidney disease often has no symptoms.
tests.general_interpretation_high: A higher ratio may suggest albumin is passing into the urine, but temporary increases can follow exercise, fever or other illness, so a repeated test is common.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.
A result outside the printed interval may or may not reflect a health problem, and a result inside the interval does not by itself guarantee health.
This explanation is general education, not a diagnosis; discuss the result with the clinician who ordered it.

tests.what_it_measures: A rheumatoid factor test measures rheumatoid factor in the blood, an antibody that attacks healthy tissue rather than germs. It is one piece of information used when assessing joint symptoms, not a diagnosis by itself.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It may be ordered when someone has joint pain, stiffness, tenderness or swelling that could suggest rheumatoid arthritis.
tests.general_interpretation_high: A positive result does not by itself diagnose rheumatoid arthritis: rheumatoid factor can be found in other conditions and in some healthy older people.
limitations: The reference interval printed on your report is specific to the laboratory that produced it; intervals from other laboratories are not interchangeable.

tests.what_it_measures: A C-reactive protein test measures CRP in the blood. The liver makes CRP in response to inflammation, which is the body's response to injury, infection or other disease.
tests.why_it_is_ordered: It may be ordered with symptoms of a bacterial infection, to monitor a chronic inflammatory condition, or to check for infection after surgery.
tests.general_interpretation_high: A raised CRP can reflect inflammation, but it does not say where the inflammation is or what caused it; the printed interval and the context guide interpretation.
